content:
Chloe Martin: heads up: for Console cost breakdown switching to Cost Model API, we need a concrete feature flag rollout plan + what happens when cost-model is sad (latency/5xx). Can we align today so we don’t block release train?

Ethan Park: yep. current plan in PR is a single server-side flag in Console backend: `console.costModelApi.enabled` (LD). When off, we use legacy breakdown (existing aggregator). When on, we call cost-model `/v1/cost:breakdown`.

Jada Williams: can we avoid “single switch flips everything” for prod? I’d prefer 2 knobs:
1) call path enabled
2) UI rendering enabled (so we can dark launch and validate payloads)

Chloe Martin: +1. dark launch first would be great.

Ethan Park: works for me. On service side we also have a “safe mode” kill switch but that’s more coarse (returns `503` with a typed error).

Rafael Mendes: from SRE POV we need an explicit fallback behavior definition. “call fails -> legacy” is ok, but watch out for partial failures + inconsistent totals. Also please put a hard timeout, don’t let Console p95 get dragged by cost-model.

Allison Grant: +1 on timeout + bounded retries. if you do retries, do them only on `connect`/`read` timeouts and *not* on 4xx.

Benji Okafor: for tenancy/auth: Console is calling as service principal + passing `org_id` as header. If the auth path breaks, we’ll see 401/403. should we fail closed (no breakdown) vs fail open (legacy)?

Jada Williams: for Console UX, I’d rather fail open to legacy. users prefer “some numbers” over empty page. but we should surface a banner if we’re showing legacy numbers (esp if they don’t match invoices).

Marissa Cole: yes pls. if fallback happens, we need a small “Using legacy cost breakdown due to service degradation” tooltip, otherwise support will get crushed.

Chloe Martin: ok so fallback plan:
- primary: cost-model breakdown
- on error/timeout: legacy breakdown + non-scary banner
- also emit metric that fallback occurred

Ethan Park: that’s reasonable. question: if cost-model returns `200` but missing fields / schema mismatch, do we treat as error?

Jada Williams: yes. if we can’t render deterministically, treat as failure and go legacy. no half-rendered tables.

Rafael Mendes: please define “missing fields” precisely. i suggest:
- if top-level `total_cost_usd` missing -> fallback
- if a particular bucket missing (e.g. overhead) -> render bucket as 0? or fallback?

Chloe Martin: for v1, the table is driven by taxonomy buckets. if a bucket missing, our totals won’t reconcile. I’d rather fallback than show misleading breakdown.

Allison Grant: agree. consistency > completeness. and you can relax in v2 once schema stabilized.

Ethan Park: k. implementation detail: cost-model response already includes `schema_version`. Console should accept `1.x` and reject `2.x` (until we upgrade). if reject -> fallback + metric.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: pls also add `x-request-id` passthrough for debugging. When Console falls back we’ll want to correlate quickly.

Chloe Martin: ack.

Connor O'Brien: release train question: can we stage rollout so we don’t need a hotfix if cost-model melts?

Ethan Park: proposal:
Phase 0 (staging): enable call path + rendering for all staging traffic, validate.
Phase 1 (prod dark launch): enable call path for 5% of requests but do NOT render (just log/metric compare).
Phase 2 (prod render canary): render for internal orgs only (Redwood dogfood org_ids) + 1-2 friendly customers.
Phase 3 (prod ramp): 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3-5 days, with abort criteria.

Rafael Mendes: define abort criteria now. at minimum:
- cost-model p95 added latency budget to Console endpoint <= 50ms
- fallback rate <= 0.5% sustained (excluding intentional schema rejects during phase)
- cost drift SLI not spiking (we can use proxy for now: difference between cost-model vs legacy totals)

Jada Williams: we can do inline diff logging during Phase 1: `abs(cost_model_total - legacy_total) / legacy_total`. We’ll sample to avoid cardinality.

Allison Grant: sampling note: please keep `org_id` out of high-cardinality logs/metrics. bucket by environment + route + model_id at most.

Benji Okafor: how do we pick “5% of requests” server-side? LD can target by user/org but not exactly request sampling unless we do consistent hashing.

Ethan Park: we can do deterministic sampling in Console backend:
`hash(org_id) % 100 < rolloutPercent` gated by LD setting. so LD just stores the percent.

Chloe Martin: perfect.

Marissa Cole: for customer comms: during Phase 2 for friendly customers, we should let CSM know there might be banner if fallback. but banner should only show when fallback triggers, not permanently.

Talia Benson: jumping in — can someone capture owners + dates? We have the Console rollout risk review next week.

Chloe Martin: owners:
- Console flags + hashing + banner + fallback metrics: Chloe/Jada (Console)
- cost-model timeout guidance + error typing: Ethan (Platform)
- SRE abort criteria + dashboard link: Rafael
- release train coordination: Connor

Rafael Mendes: timeout recommendation:
- client timeout 150ms (hard)
- no retries on 5xx (we don’t want amplify); 1 retry only on connect timeout w/ jittered backoff 10-20ms
- circuit breaker: if we see >5% 5xx over 1 min, auto-disable via LD? (at least page oncall)

Ethan Park: auto-disable via LD is a little spicy (permissions / audit). but we can do “soft breaker”: if error rate high, Console immediately falls back without calling cost-model for 60s (local in-memory). That reduces blast radius.

Jada Williams: +1 soft breaker in Console. We can implement: if `consecutive_failures >= 20` then open breaker for 60s.

Allison Grant: make sure breaker state is per-instance; don’t try to coordinate across fleet.

Benji Okafor: also: when breaker open, still emit metric `breaker_open=1` so we can see it.

Chloe Martin: banner behavior:
- only show if we used legacy fallback for that request
- text: “Cost breakdown temporarily using legacy estimator due to service degradation. Totals may differ from invoice.”
- include request-id in “copy details” for support

Marissa Cole: wording ok. maybe remove “invoice” mention? it scares ppl.

Chloe Martin: fair. how about: “Totals may differ from other reports.”

Marissa Cole: better.

Connor O'Brien: timeline: can we land flag plumbing this week so we can ship in next train behind default-off?

Chloe Martin: yes. PR already has base flag, we’ll split into two:
- `console.costModelApi.callPercent` (int 0-100)
- `console.costModelApi.renderEnabled` (bool)
Default `0` + `false` in prod.

Ethan Park: cost-model side: we’ll ensure `503 COST_MODEL_DEGRADED` is returned when we trip service safe mode, so Console can classify. but Console should treat any non-200 as fallback.

Rafael Mendes: also handle slow success: if request hits timeout, you cancel and fallback. ok.

LaunchDarkly Bot: LaunchDarkly flag created: console.costModelApi.callPercent (default: 0). Requested by Chloe Martin.

LaunchDarkly Bot: LaunchDarkly flag created: console.costModelApi.renderEnabled (default: false). Requested by Chloe Martin.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: please document in internal runbook where to flip the flags + who has perms.

Talia Benson: I’ll add to rollout checklist doc. Ethan/Chloe, pls send me the final abort criteria + banner copy once locked.

Ethan Park: will do. I’ll also add a short section to the incident runbook: “Console fallback spike” with what to check (cost-model p95, 5xx, telemetry lag).

Chloe Martin: cool. last question: if cost-model is returning partial breakdown due to bounded response (e.g. too many segments), will we ever see 200 but truncated?

Ethan Park: v1 contract: if we truncate, we still include `truncated=true` + `truncation_reason`. Console should treat `truncated=true` as fallback for now.

Jada Williams: agreed. we can revisit later.

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: from me. please make sure metrics are tagged with `fallback_reason` (timeout, non_200, schema_reject, truncated, breaker_open) but keep the tag cardinality low.

Chloe Martin: got it. thanks all.
